title: Genetic Diseases and Inheritance
text: Genetic diseases are disorders caused by abnormalities in an individual's genome. They can be classified as single-gene (Mendelian) disorders, chromosomal disorders, or multifactorial disorders. Single-gene disorders follow inheritance patterns: autosomal dominant (one mutated copy causes disease, e.g., Huntington's), autosomal recessive (two mutated copies needed, e.g., cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease), and X-linked (gene on X chromosome, e.g., hemophilia). Down syndrome is a chromosomal disorder caused by trisomy 21 (three copies of chromosome 21). Genetic testing can identify many disorders prenatally or in early life. Gene therapy aims to treat genetic diseases by correcting mutated genes.
